name: Datum Schema
tagline: Intelligent P&IDs and process flow diagrams: draw, check and list.
for: Process, chemical, mechanical, piping and instrument engineers, operators and students.
about: Datum Schema draws piping and instrument diagrams where every symbol and line carries its data and knows what it is connected to. You place real symbols (vessels, pumps, exchangers, valves, instruments) and join them with lines that route themselves; drop a valve on a line and it goes into it, carry a line to another sheet with a pair of off-page connectors.

Because the drawing knows its connections, Datum Schema writes the line list, the equipment list, the instrument index and the valve list for you, always in step with the drawing; it checks the drawing as you work (duplicate tags, open ends, size changes without a reducer, pumps without check valves and more); and it sizes every line, with its velocity and pressure drop against limits for its service. Hydraulic results are a sizing aid, checked by the engineer.

Every symbol is a view of a plant object (equipment, valve, instrument, line number) in a plant › unit › area hierarchy, defined by a class library you can extend with your company's attributes. Every change is recorded in the project file, and every piece of equipment, instrument, control valve and relief device has a datasheet whose process conditions come straight from the P&ID.

Process flow diagrams sit beside the P&IDs: streams with their flows and conditions, a stream table on the sheet, and heat and mass balance checks. A client's legend sheet (DXF) becomes a symbol library to draw a project to their standard; an old drawing can sit behind a sheet to trace over; issued sheets are compared and the changes clouded. Lines go to Datum Pipe for stress analysis and control loops to Datum Sim for tuning.

steps.title: Draw the plant
steps.text: Drag symbols from the palette and draw lines port to port. In-line valves and fittings split the line they are dropped on; off-page connectors carry lines between sheets.

steps.title: Check it as you go
steps.text: Twenty-seven rules run on every change: duplicate tags, open ends, size and class changes, check valves, relief paths, control loops, velocities and pressure drops, heat, mass and component balances on process flow diagrams, instrument ranges, loop wiring pipe specs, instrument wiring and your company's own rules. Click an issue to go to it, or choose one of its fixes.

steps.title: Print the drawings and lists
steps.text: Print the sheets to PDF with their border and title block, export DXF for any CAD program, and the line list, equipment list, instrument index and valve list to Excel or CSV.

highlights: About 80 symbols of our own, following ISO 10628-2 and ISA-5.1
Process flow diagrams: streams in diamonds, a stream table on the sheet, heat and mass balance checks
A client's legend (DXF) becomes a symbol library; draw a project to their standard and back
Old drawings (DXF) behind a sheet to trace over; revision clouds round what changed since an issue
Send a line to Datum Pipe, a control loop to Datum Sim, and equipment and lines to Datum Calc as calculation sheets
Sizing of control valves (IEC 60534-2-1), orifice plates (ISO 5167-2) and relief valves (API 520), written to their datasheets
Stream compositions with a component balance; an I/O summary per control system with spare
Instrument wiring: junction boxes, cables and I/O cards; a cable schedule and the I/O allocation
A valve and fitting take-off by type, size, pipe class and rating
Your company's title block: its cells, fields and logo, shared as a file
Pipe specs: classes with the components they allow, read from CSV; checks and a take-off with commodity codes
Review comments pinned to the drawing, with replies; reviewers' copies merged back in
Plant objects in a plant › unit › area hierarchy; symbols are views, every change is recorded
A class library you can extend with your company's attributes

Equipment and instrument datasheets with process conditions from the P&ID; stream results imported from a simulator (Excel, CSV); revisions with what changed (Δ); your company's form; import from Excel; print and Excel
Loop diagrams drawn from the P&ID, with junction box, cable and I/O wiring
Cause-and-effect matrix read from the interlocks on the P&ID
Lines route themselves at right angles, hop over each other and carry flow arrows
A valve dropped on a line splits it and joins both halves
Off-page connectors pair across sheets; click one to jump to its partner
A first P&ID developed from the process flow diagram, and a process flow diagram made from P&IDs drawn first
A tag register: tags added before they are drawn, every tag's status
Process cases (normal, maximum, minimum and your own) that the hydraulics, sizing and datasheets follow
Standard arrangements round equipment placed in one step, editable by your company
Live line list, equipment list, instrument index, valve list and datasheet index, and reports you design yourself
Twenty-seven checks, including balances, instrument ranges, pipe specs, wiring and your own rules, each with a click to the problem
Line hydraulics: velocity, Reynolds number, Colebrook friction factor and pressure drop against limits
SI and US units; DXF, SVG, PDF, Excel, CSV and the DEXPI P&ID exchange format (export and import)
Automatic tags and loop numbers, renumbering, a legend sheet
A user guide in the app: every feature step by step, searchable and printable

roadmap.title: Piping rules
items: 0.4.0: pipe specs: each pipe class lists the components it allows, by size and rating; spec checks (done)
0.4.1: values passed along a line (size and class to its valves and fittings) and a to-do list after changes (done)
0.4.2: implied items (flanges, gaskets, bolts) in the take-off (done)
0.4.3: assemblies (a group placed as one) and data labels you choose on the drawing (done)
0.4.4: rules and tag formats of your own; speed on large projects (done)

roadmap.title: Instruments and calculations
items: 0.5.0: instrument wiring: cables, junction boxes, terminals, I/O cards, cable schedule; loop diagrams from them (done)
0.5.1: calculation sheets in Datum Calc from an object's data (pump power and NPSH, line pressure drop, exchanger, vessel wall) (done)
0.5.2: sizing of control valves, orifices and relief valves (done)
0.5.3: equipment datasheets; stream tables imported from simulator results (Excel, CSV) (done)
0.5.4: reports you design yourself: columns, filters and grouping, saved and exported (done)

roadmap.title: From PFD to P&ID and back
items: 0.6.0: standard arrangements by equipment type (a pump's valves, strainer and gauge; a vessel's relief and level loop), editable by your company (done)
0.6.1: develop a P&ID from the PFD: the same equipment, streams become line numbers with their data, sizes and classes suggested, arrangements placed, routed as a draft (done)
0.6.2: make a PFD from the P&IDs: main equipment and process streams, valves and instruments left out (done)
0.6.3: PFD and P&ID kept in step both ways: a change on either side shows on the other's to-do list (done)
0.6.4: process cases (normal, maximum, minimum, design) on streams, lines and datasheets (done)
0.6.5: a tag register: tags created and imported before they are drawn (done)

roadmap.title: Deeper P&IDs
items: 0.7.0: insulation and heat tracing on every line: type, thickness, tracing medium, breaks, in the line number and lists, with checks (done)
0.7.1: fixes offered for the checks (insert the missing check valve or reducer, take a neighbour's size, renumber a duplicate) and the problems clouded on the sheet (done)
0.7.2: every list and report edited in Excel and read back, with a preview first (done)
0.7.3: control loops placed in one step (flow, level, pressure, temperature) and valves drawn open or closed (done)
0.7.4: safety analysis: the protections each kind of equipment needs (high and low pressure and level, relief), checked and tabulated (done)
0.7.5: an electrical load list from the equipment, and how complete every class's data is (done)

roadmap.title: Drawing breadth
items: 0.8.0: nozzles you add and place on equipment, with their size, rating and service (done)
0.8.1: a symbol swapped for another keeping its tag, data and connections; copies of a spare take the next suffix (P-101A, P-101B) (done)
0.8.2: a second built-in symbol set, chosen per project (done)
0.8.3: a sheet manager: sheets listed with their status, batch printing, and deleted sheets recovered (done)

roadmap.title: Beyond the drawing
items: 0.9.0: an isolation planner: the valves to close and the drains and vents to open to isolate a piece of equipment, shown and listed
0.9.1: the plant as one interactive web page anyone can open: click a tag to see its data
0.9.2: HAZOP support: nodes marked on the P&ID and worksheets linked to its lines and equipment, safeguards filled from the drawing
0.9.3: pressure test packs: test boundaries on the P&ID and the test pack list
0.9.4: a handover package: tags, classes, data and documents in a structured export

roadmap.title: Teams
items: 0.10.0: document status (for review, approval, construction), approvals and transmittals
0.10.1: shared projects: several people, items claimed, tag numbers reserved, work merged
0.10.2: old DXF P&IDs turned into live drawings: blocks mapped to symbols, lines traced and connected
0.10.3: scripting; more CAD drawing formats

roadmap.title: Ready for 3D
items: 0.11.0: a plant package for 3D modelling: equipment with its datasheet values and nozzles, each line with its ends, size, spec, insulation and components in order, in an open, documented format
0.11.1: a P&ID compared with a 3D model's or isometric's data: missing items, sizes and order along each line
